Definition: a nude place, i.e. (literally) the pudenda, or (figuratively) a vacant space
BiblicalUsage: The word names a bare or open place, and its two uses could hardly be further apart. On the bronze bases of the temple it marks the open space around the carved cherubim and lions, measured out in proportion, while Nahum turns it against Nineveh, saying God will show the nations her nakedness and the kingdoms her shame.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that what is bare before God is either beautiful or shameful, and the difference is whether He has covered it or we have uncovered it ourselves.
